title: Customer Need Spectrometer — Rapid Synthesis (Oct 2026)
body:
Purpose:
Quick, engineering-actionable synthesis of recent customer voices (week of 2026-10-01 -> 2026-10-04). The "spectrometer" metaphor: separate strong signals from background noise so we can ship low-risk, high-impact patches this quarter. This is a working artefact — notes, rough estimates, and open questions included.

How this doc was made:
- Pulled 27 discrete tickets / call notes (CS calls, support threads, pilot check-ins).
- Listened to recorded calls from three Tier-1 customers (anonymized quotes below).
- Cross-referenced recent runtime incidents and a small sampling of SDK bug reports.

Top emergent themes (ranked by severity x frequency):
1) Latency unpredictability for short-chat workloads (~25 mentions) — customers care about 90th percentile spikes during bursts even if median is fine.
2) KV/prefix-cache surprises (~18 mentions) — users accidentally double-send prefixes or rely on opaque caching that changes output.
3) Cost visibility per-route and per-feature (~14 mentions) — teams want cost breaking by model variant + cache hit/miss.
4) Model-fallback transparency (~9 mentions) — when we fallback to smaller model, downstream app behaviour changes and teams want deterministic signals.
5) Console ergonomics for rollout controls (~11 mentions) — canary configs, easy revert, and rollout metrics near the button.

Representative customer quotes (anonymized):
- "We saw a 300ms jitter on the 95th percentile during our morning sync. It breaks our typing UX because the client shows multiple transient states."
- "The cache did something weird — sometimes our first prompt got cached and later prompts used stale context. We couldn't tell why."
- "Why did the model switch at 3am? We got a different tone and had to roll back manually."

Quick wins (low effort, high user-perceived impact):
A) Latency badge on console and API header (ETA: 1 sprint)
   - Show live 95th/99th latency and a simple color badge for the route.
   - Implementation: console front-end + expose per-route metric in /routes API (non-breaking).
   - Owner: Rina (CS) + Console eng (small).

B) KV-cache 'explain' toggle in logs (ETA: 1 sprint)
   - On a request, include a boolean + small fingerprint saying whether prefix/KV cache was used and which key-range matched. No user data payloads — just metadata.
   - Customer benefit: reduces guesswork, allows deterministic debugging.
   - Privacy: metadata only.
   - Owner: Connor (Infra) + Applied-ML consult.

C) Per-route cost snapshot export (ETA: 2 sprints)
   - CSV with tokens, model-variant used, caching ratio, and estimated $ per bucket.
   - Useful for finance and product managers.
   - Owner: Evan (CS analytics) + Billing eng.

Medium-impact experiments (medium effort):
D) Canary transparency panel (ETA: 3–4 sprints)
   - When a rollout is active, show traffic split, per-variant perf and a one-click rollback.
   - Add event hooks to notify webhooks on swap/rollback.
   - Risk: requires backend support for metric rollups per rollout window.

E) Fallback explanation header (ETA: 3 sprints)
   - When routing policy triggers fallback (cost/latency), return header like X-Redwood-Fallback: model-x -> model-y; reason=capacity.
   - Helps teams conditionally handle format/quality changes.

Large / strategic asks (schedule into roadmap if validated):
F) Simulation mode in console for rollout impact (ETA: 6+ sprints)
   - Run synthetic traffic overlay to preview latency/cost for a proposed rollout size.
   - Would reduce risk for large customers shifting models.

G) SKU-level cost attribution + anomaly alerts (ETA: 5+ sprints)
   - Auto-alert when per-route $ spikes > 25% week-over-week with root-cause hints (cache ratio drop, model change, token-length shift).

Rough triage matrix (frequency vs. engineering effort):
- Latency badge: freq high, effort low -> ship first.
- KV explain: freq medium, effort low -> ship alongside badge.
- Cost snapshot: freq medium, effort medium -> next.
- Canary panel / fallback headers: freq medium, effort medium-high -> Q1/next quarter projects.

Metrics to measure impact (post-deploy):
- Reduction in CS tickets mentioning "unclear cache" (target 50% drop in 8 weeks).
- Time-to-diagnose for latency incidents (median down from ~3h -> 45m).
- Adoption of per-route CSV by finance teams (download counts).

Open questions and risks:
- How much metadata can we expose without leaking customer inputs? (security review needed).
- Are there storage costs for per-request cache fingerprints at scale? (infra needs estimate).
- Will the fallback header create brittle client-side logic if customers code to headers? Suggest: include a deprecation/contract note in the header docs.

Proposed next steps (week by week):
Week 0 (this week): sync with Console PM + Infra lead, validate privacy constraints.
Week 1: spike on KV fingerprint storage (infra), small UX mock for latency badge (design).
Week 2: ship latency badge + basic API header for route metrics behind feature flag to 20% internal org traffic.
Week 3–4: iterate on KV explain + export CSV for a small pilot customer (pilot list attached below).

Pilot customers (interested, opt-in):
- "AlphaRetail" (tokenized commerce chat app) — strong need for latency badge.
- "LegalFlow" (document summarization) — cares about fallback determinism.
- "ScribeX" (note-taking app) — interested in cost snapshot.

Unresolved/Notes to self:
- Confirm billing calc model with finance (per-token vs. amortized model variants).
- File privacy assessment request: security@redwood (ticket created: SEC-2026-99).
- Draft a short customer-facing blurb for pilots that sets expectations (who will see metadata, retention window, how to opt-out).

Appendix: quick timeline estimate for first three artifacts
- Latency badge & route metrics API: 2 weeks (design + 1 backend + 1 frontend sprint).
- KV-cache explain: 2 weeks (small server side change + add header).
- Per-route cost CSV: 3 weeks (billing join + export endpoint + small UI).

If you read only one thing: ship the latency badge + KV explain. Both are low-risk, unblock >30% of current "where did the jitter come from" tickets, and provide quick wins for customers and CS.

Questions for the engineering sync:
- Infra: estimated storage + QPS overhead for emitting KV fingerprints?
- Console: can we place a badge without changing the whole route page layout?
- Billing: are there pre-existing endpoints to join tokens -> $ that we can reuse?

-- end of rapid synthesis --
